label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 15
knowledgePattern: Negate a supplied divisibility definition while retaining distinct partners
solution:
The definition first demands success for every member x. Its negation therefore requires at least one member x for which success is impossible.

For that chosen x, no permitted pair of distinct other members y,z can have any common prime divisor with x. Equivalently, every allowed pair y,z has no prime dividing all three numbers.

This is exactly D. The distinctness conditions stay in place throughout. Saying that no prime divides all three is not the same as demanding a prime dividing x but neither of the other two.

hints.title: Separate the three choices
hints.body: Write the definition on three lines: the condition on x; the choice of y and z; the choice of prime p.
hints.recap: Later choices are made for the x already chosen.
hints.pitfall: Keep y and z distinct from each other and from x.
hints.pause: Identify where the definition says “every” and where it says “there exist”.

recall.reminder: Preserve the order and restrictions in a supplied definition.

hints.title: Negate one line at a time
hints.body: Start at the outermost condition. “Every” fails when at least one allowed choice fails; “there exists” fails when every allowed choice fails.
hints.recap: Change the quantifier, then negate what remains inside it.
hints.pitfall: Failing one partner pair is not the same as having no successful pair.
hints.pause: Write the full negation, keeping the original restrictions, and compare it with the options.

recall.reminder: Negate from the outside inward without changing the domains.
